confirmed.title: After the merge, the ground code joins solids within 0.01 ft (TOL), but #18 treats anything within 0.1 ft (TOUCH) as part of the main building. A balcony drawn 0.05 ft off the wall makes every yard and the height stop with "doesn't meet the buildings"
confirmed.detail: #18 decided that a solid within TOUCH = 0.1 ft of the main building is part of it (_touching/_attached, §325-18A: porch, balcony, steps). The ground code brought in from term-index (_connected, which feeds _meets_ground, `home` = _grade_home/_joined_ids, _separate_grade and _raised_by_shape) only joins solids within TOL = 0.01 ft. term-index has no TOUCH, so the gap is only visible in #18. Example: a balcony 0.05 ft off the house wall with spot grades. #18 counts it in parts_of, so the yards measure it as part of the house. But _meets_ground tests it as its own group, finds it 'floating', and every yard, the building area and the height stop with the wrong words: "the ground level (0.0 ft) doesn't meet the buildings (they run from 10.0 to 10.5 ft)". This is #15 round 5's balcony fix undone for any gap between 0.01 and 0.1 ft. The same mismatch puts such a solid outside `home`: it gets cut at its own grade (_at_ground) and judged for 'buried' against its own ground (_ground_against), while #18 calls it part of the main building that the fc2cfd8 merge says is read at the grade plane. No false pass (the result is needs review), but an architect sees a wrong, blocking reason on an ordinary drawing.
confirmed.evidence: measure.py:1505 `_footprint(o).distance(plan) <= TOL for o in g)]` (TOL = 0.01, line 35) against measure.py:2009 `plans[b["id"]].distance(grown) <= TOUCH` (TOUCH = 0.1, line 51: "a solid this close to the main building (in plan) is part of it"). Run on HEAD: house = 3 floor blocks (10,25)-(35,65); balcony box(35+gap,26,40,34,10,10.5); spots [[22,24,0],[22,66,0],[9,45,0],[36,45,0],[36,27,0]]; ground_is_flat None. gap=0.0: front_yard 25.0. gap=0.05: front_yard None, reason "the ground level (0.0 ft) doesn't meet the buildings (they run from 10.0 to 10.5 ft): check the ground level"; building_height stops with the same reason.
confirmed.pin: packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py::test_a_balcony_against_the_house_is_part_of_it_for_the_ground_wherever_the_spot_grades_are, extended with a gap of 0.05 ft (balcony box(35.05, at, 40, at+8, 10, 10.5)): asserts front_yard is measured (a value or readings) and 'doesn't meet the buildings' is not in its reason. Fails on HEAD.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use one 'touching' test. Have _connected join groups by `_footprint(o).distance(plan) <= TOUCH`, the same threshold as _touching/_attached, or build the plan-touching part of _connected from _touching. Then the ground model's groups, `home` and parts_of always agree. Keep the stacked (one over another) joining as it is.
skeptics: The finding holds. measure.py:1505 (`_connected`) joins two solids only when their footprints are within TOL (0.01 ft, line 35). The main-building join added in #18, at lines 1999-2009 (`_touching`/`_attached`), uses TOUCH (0.1 ft, line 51). a7a0be0 has no TOUCH at all, so the two different distances exist only on HEAD. `_meets_ground` (1511-1524) goes through `_connected`, and so do `_joined_ids`/`_grade_home` (1466-1480) and `_separate_grade` (1487-1495). That means a solid between 0.01 and 0.1 ft from the house is checked against the ground as its own group. I ran the reviewer's case on HEAD with uv and pytest: 3 floor blocks (10,25)-(35,65), a balcony box at (35+gap, 26, 40, 34) from z 10 to 10.5, the five spot grades given, ground_is_flat None, main_building "floor 1". At gap 0.0 and 0.005, front_yard is 25.0. At gap 0.05 and 0.09, front_yard is None and building_height stops with "the ground level (0.0 ft) doesn't meet the buildings (they run from 10.0 to 10.5 ft): check the ground level". So the wrong blocking reason is real. It is never a false pass: the result is "needs review" with the wrong explanation. I found no earlier check that brings the two distances into line.

I could not refute this finding. I read the code and reproduced the failure on HEAD (fc2cfd8). In measure.py, line 35 sets TOL = 0.01 and line 51 sets TOUCH = 0.1. _connected (lines 1498-1508) joins solids only when `_footprint(o).distance(plan) <= TOL`. _touching/_attached (lines 1998-2012) join a solid to the main building when `plans[b["id"]].distance(grown) <= TOUCH`. _meets_ground (lines 1511-1524) checks each _connected group separately. _joined_ids, _grade_home and _separate_grade (lines 1466-1495) also build on _connected. So a solid 0.01 to 0.1 ft away counts as part of the main building for the yards but as a separate building for the ground test. I ran the reviewer's case (three floor blocks (10,25)-(35,65), balcony box(35+gap,26,40,34,10,10.5), the five spot grades, ground_is_flat None) using uv with pytest. At gap 0.0 and 0.005, front_yard is 25.0. At gap 0.05, front_yard is None and the reason is "the ground level (0.0 ft) doesn't meet the buildings (they run from 10.0 to 10.5 ft): check the ground level". building_height stops with the same reason. No upstream check stops this, and the existing balcony test (test_measure.py:1833) only covers gap 0. One detail on where it comes from: a7a0be0 (term-index) has _connected but no TOUCH. #18's own first parent (fc2cfd8^1) already had both, with _connected using TOL. So the mismatch is not new in the last merge commit, but it is part of the a7a0be0...HEAD diff under review, and the behavior is real. The result is needs review (no false pass), but the reason it gives is wrong, so P2 fits.

confirmed.title: In the port, #15 round 10's 'main building's parts cut at the grade plane' test lost its pin. Reverting the fix in _at_ground fails no test, yet it adds a made-up projection question to the rear yard
confirmed.detail: #15 round 10 (2) pinned the ground cut for the main building's own parts at the §325-3 grade plane, not at the average of its corners, by asserting the building area had no made-up 'overhangs' reading. Under #18 the building area is always from above (coverage_seen_from_above). So the adapted assertions (`area == 1000` and `'overhangs' not in reason`) hold whatever the cut is. Under #18 the cut shows up in the yards' walls-at-ground reading, and the test never looks there. Mutation: changing measure.py:322 to `level = sum(ground) / len(ground)` (dropping `plan_level if _is_home(...)`) still passes the whole model_measurement suite. On the 'stepped' case, though, rear_yard goes from a value of 35.0 to None with readings [35.0, 55.0 'to its walls at ground level, what sticks out above being a bay window…'], a needs-review that shouldn't be there. One of #15's intended behaviours is now unprotected.
confirmed.evidence: test: `area = stepped["building_area"]; assert area["value"] == pytest.approx(1000.0) or ... ; assert "overhangs" not in (area["reason"] or "")`, and building_area is _coverage's from-above union (measure.py:2100). Mutant measure.py:322 `level = sum(ground) / len(ground)`: `pytest packages/model_measurement` all pass. Stepped case on HEAD: rear_yard 35.0, no readings. Mutant: rear_yard None, readings [('',35.0),('to its walls at ground level, what sticks out above being a …',55.0)].
confirmed.pin: In test_the_main_buildings_own_parts_are_read_against_its_grade_plane_never_their_own_corners, add `assert _walls_reading(stepped, "rear_yard") is None and stepped["rear_yard"]["value"] == pytest.approx(35.0)`. It must fail with measure.py:322 reverted to the average of the corners.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the adapted test assert what #15 round 10 (2) protects as it appears under #18: no walls-at-ground (projection) reading on any yard of the stepped house, and rear_yard == 35. Do this the way test_every_known_shape_is_read_at_the_ground_as_it_should_be_all_at_once was moved over to the yards.

priorStatus.title: After the merge, a walls-only object stops every measurement with an unnamed 'isn't a closed solid' and nothing is highlighted. Round 22's naming now only works when the check is monkeypatched off
priorStatus.reasoning: Read the fix. _unenclosed/read_3dm now name the object (`stop("open_solid", what=_called(building))`). measure() (measure.py:1677-1683) adds _open_ids to `objects` on every row that is waiting with the open_solid prefix, and keeps that row's own ids (dict.fromkeys merge). _measure works out `opened`/`only_open`/`placed`, so the off-lot reason is still given next to the open object when the open object is the only problem: coverage via both(why_building, unplaced(buildings)); main yards via both(why_building, why_main_off) with objects=unplaced_ids(group); accessory yards via both(why_building, why_acc_off). The open object itself is never placed. The 'flat' branches are deleted, and they are truly unreachable: an empty projection means _unenclosed returns open_solid at k=2, or the object already has reader problems, so why_building is set and views is {}. The test no longer monkeypatches and passes (the model_measurement suite passes on HEAD). Pre-existing, not in this branch: an open mesh's reader stop 'open_mesh' (read_3dm.py:222, term-index) is neither named nor picked up by _open_ids, so it is still unhighlighted. That gap belongs to term-index.
